title: Two independently certified private HTTPS services and mandatory mTLS
summary: The owner private CA issues distinct NOC and Office server leaf certificates. Approved browsers trust the private CA; each authorized device additionally holds an individually issued client certificate. Server-side client-certificate validation is the access gate, before LDAP/Access Permissions.
invariants: NOC certificate covers noc.rasenfalcon.com, irrespective of DNS CNAME; Office certificate covers office.rasenfalcon.com.
Two separate server private keys, systemd units and service users; no public shared vhost.
No cert, wrong CA, incorrect EKU, expired or revoked device certificate must fail during handshake.
Reject missing/unknown SNI and SNI/Host mismatch; absent issuer or failed rotation must fail closed.
FORBID public CA or ACME fallback, password-only admission, anonymous TLS, plaintext HTTP, default shared vhost and untrusted reverse proxy.
Only owner-approved devices get the private CA trust anchor and a separate device client identity; never ship private root or server keys in source.
Real positive and negative TLS handshakes are required before reporting live readiness.

provenance.claim: Binding owner private HTTPS security directive, not installed.
